mainTopic: Who keeps the extra profit when a שליח gets a better deal, and what happens when a שליח sells more than he was asked to
overview: The גמרא learns from our משנה that רבי holds that any extra gain from a deal belongs to the owner of the money (בעל המעות). It brings a ברייתא where רבי יהודה gives an extra item to the שליח and רבי יוסי says they split it. Another ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי as giving everything to the owner. רמי בר חמא resolves the contradiction: for an item with a fixed price (קצבה) they split, and for an item without one everything goes to the owner. רב פפא rules that this is the הלכה. The גמרא then asks a new question: if someone told his שליח to sell a לתך and he sold a כור, is the שליח adding to his instructions, so the לתך is sold, or going against them, so nothing is sold? A proof from a host, his שליח and guests who took too much הקדש meat is rejected. A second proof from our משנה about a widow who sold too much land is also rejected, because she may simply have sold too cheaply.

steps.title: Our משנה shows רבי's view: the profit goes to the owner of the money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from our משנה that רבי holds that all extra gain belongs to בעל המעות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, in our משנה, רבי taught that everything belongs to the owner of the money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that our משנה reveals רבי's opinion: if a deal brings in extra, it all belongs to the owner of the money, not to the one who made the deal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה ruled that the extra gain from a sale goes to the owner. The גמרא turns that ruling into a general principle in רבי's name. This sets up the question of where this principle fits in an older argument between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Here רבי taught; our משנה shows רבי's opinion
Everything goes to the owner of the money
The owner of the money, the one who sent the agent

phrases.english: Here Rabbi taught,
phrases.notes: "Here" means in our משנה; רבי is רבי יהודה הנשיא, who put the משנה together.

phrases.english: everything belongs to the owner of the money,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general principle out of the משנה just learned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי, extra gain from a deal belongs entirely to בעל המעות.

steps.title: The ברייתא where רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי argue about an extra item
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing this is an older argument: רבי יהודה gives the extra item to the שליח, and רבי יוסי says they split it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: if the seller added one extra item for the agent, it all goes to the agent, says רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי says: they split it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the question of who gets the extra was already argued about by תנאים, so we can see where רבי's view stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An agent buys for his sender, and the seller throws in one extra item. רבי יהודה says the agent keeps it all, and in this ברייתא רבי יוסי says the agent and the owner split it. The next step brings another ברייתא in which רבי יוסי says everything goes to the owner, which is exactly רבי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
They added one extra item for him
Agent who acts for someone else
They split it

phrases.english: as it is taught: If they added for him one extra item,
phrases.notes: The case is an agent sent to buy, and the seller gives him one more item than he paid for.

phrases.english: everything goes to the agent; these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Yosei says: They split it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the ברייתא that shows the background argument for רבי's view.
steps.raayaObject: That the question of who gets extra gain from an agent's deal is an argument among תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the argument between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי.

steps.title: Another ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: another ברייתא says רבי יוסי holds that everything goes to the owner of the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: But another ברייתא teaches that רבי יוסי says: everything belongs to the owner of the money!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction: one ברייתא says רבי יוסי splits the extra, and another says he gives it all to the owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both quotes are in רבי יוסי's name, yet they give different rulings. The גמרא needs to explain how one תנא could say both things.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא; a challenge from another source

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: Rabbi Yosei says:
Everything belongs to the owner of the money!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the version of רבי יוסי's view quoted in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's ruling of חולקין in the first ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי as giving everything to the owner, which contradicts his ruling to split.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא: fixed-price items versus items without a fixed price
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא answers that the two quotes of רבי יוסי deal with different kinds of items: with a fixed price (קצבה) or without one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: It is not difficult. Here it is talking about an item with a fixed price; there it is talking about an item without a fixed price.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא resolves the contradiction by saying each ברייתא is talking about a different kind of item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When an item has a fixed price, an extra item is clearly a gift, and we don't know if it was meant for the agent or the owner, so they split it. When there is no fixed price, the extra is just part of a better deal, so it belongs to the owner of the money. So רבי יוסי never really contradicts himself.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the contradiction can be resolved
A fixed, set price
An item that has a fixed price

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: לָא קַשְׁיָא.
phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama said: It is not difficult.
Here it is about an item that has a fixed price,
phrases.notes: This matches the ברייתא where they split, since the extra is clearly a gift.

phrases.english: there it is about an item that has no fixed price.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source deals with a different kind of item.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי יוסי gave two opposite rulings on the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Fixed-price item: they split. Item without a fixed price: everything goes to the owner of the money.

steps.title: רב פפא rules the הלכה follows this distinction
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that for a fixed-price item they split, and for an item without a fixed price everything goes to the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The הלכה is: an item with a fixed price, they split; an item without a fixed price, everything goes to the owner of the money.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the practical ruling, using exactly the distinction רמי בר חמא made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא turns רמי בר חמא's answer into actual הלכה. His wording sounds just like what was already said, which leads straight to the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical הלכה; the final ruling

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: The halakha is:
an item that has a fixed price — they split it,

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין לוֹ קִצְבָה — הַכֹּל לְבַעַל הַמָּעוֹת.
phrases.english: an item that has no fixed price — everything goes to the owner of the money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer of step 4 into the practical ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Fixed-price item: the extra is split. No fixed price: the extra all goes to בעל המעות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical rule for anyone who sends an agent and the agent ends up with something extra.

steps.title: What new thing is רב פפא teaching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב פפא adds, since רמי בר חמא already said this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב פפא needed to say anything, because his words just repeat רמי בר חמא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא expects every statement to add something new. Since רב פפא's ruling looks identical to step 4, the גמרא wants to know what it adds.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? What does this add?

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the need for רב פפא's ruling in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רב פפא's ruling adds beyond רמי בר חמא's answer.

steps.title: The answer we gave is a real answer you can rule by
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא is teaching that רמי בר חמא's distinction is not just a way to settle a contradiction, but the true הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The answer that we answered is a true answer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רב פפא is confirming that רמי בר חמא's answer is correct and can be used for practical rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sometimes a תירוץ is only a possible way to settle a contradiction, not something you would rule by. רב פפא is telling us this one is the real thing, and we decide cases based on it.

keyTerms.meaning: An answer that settles a contradiction
That we answered

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב פפא added a new law here. The law is the same as step 4; what's new is that the answer is confirmed as the real, practical הלכה.

phrases.english: The answer that we answered is a true answer.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב פפא confirms that רמי בר חמא's distinction is the true, practical הלכה.
steps.whatToRemember: An extra item goes to the owner of the money if the item has no fixed price, and is split if it has a fixed price. רב פפא confirms this is the הלכה.

steps.title: Told to sell a לתך, the שליח sold a כור: is even the לתך sold?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: if a שליח sells more than he was told, did he add to his sender's words (so the לתך is sold), or go against them (so nothing is sold)?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: If someone said to his agent, 'Sell a לתך for me,' and he went and sold a כור for him, what is the law? Is he adding to his words, so at least the לתך is acquired? Or maybe he is going against his words, so even the לתך is not acquired?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about a שליח who sold double what he was told to sell, and lays out both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A לתך is half a כור, so the שליח did what he was asked and then more. One side says he did his job plus extra, so the half he was sent for counts. The other side says he did not follow his instructions at all, so the whole sale is his own doing and even the לתך is not sold.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the חכמים
A לתך, half a כור
A כור, a large dry measure
Adding to his sender's words; did the job plus more
Going against his sender's words; did not follow instructions

phrases.english: A question was raised before them: If he said to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is the agent; the owner is giving instructions.

phrases.english: Sell a half-kor for me,
and he went and sold a kor for him, what is the law?
Is he adding to his words,
and at least the half-kor is acquired,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא מַעֲבִיר עַל דְּבָרָיו הוּא,
phrases.english: or perhaps he is going against his words,
and even the half-kor is not acquired?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about a שליח who goes beyond his instructions.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a שליח who sells more than told counts as adding to his instructions (the לתך is sold) or going against them (nothing is sold).
steps.whyThisMatters: This question decides how far a שליח can stray from his instructions before his whole act stops counting for the sender.

steps.title: A proof from the case of the host, the agent, and the guests
steps.stepSummary: רב יעקב מנהר פקוד, quoting רבינא, brings a משנה: a host told his שליח to give the guests one piece, the שליח told them to take two, they took three, and all of them are guilty of מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יעקב מנהר פקוד said in the name of רבינא: Come and hear. If the host told his agent, 'Give the guests a piece,' and the agent told them, 'Take two,' and they took three, then all of them are guilty of misusing הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to answer the question from Step 8. In this step it only quotes the case; the reasoning comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a case where a שליח told the guests to take more than his sender said, which is exactly our question. The striking detail is that even the host is guilty of מעילה. That means the host's instruction still counted, even though the שליח changed it.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source to settle the question
The host or owner, here the one who sends the שליח
They are guilty of מעילה, misusing property that belongs to הקדש
Guests

phrases.english: Rav Ya'akov of the Pekod River said
in the name of Ravina:
Come and hear:
The host said to his agent:
"Give them a piece, to the guests,"
and he (the agent) says: "Take two,"
and they took three
all of them are guilty of misusing הקדש.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, אָמַר בַּעַל הַבַּיִת לִשְׁלוּחוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to settle the question asked in Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That a שליח who does more than he was told is מוסיף על דבריו, so his act still counts for the sender.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מעילה about the host, the שליח, and the guests: all are guilty.

steps.title: Why the host is guilty only if the agent is 'adding'
steps.stepSummary: If the שליח is 'adding to his words,' it makes sense that the host is guilty. If he is 'going against his words,' the host should not be guilty, because a שליח who does not do his mission makes himself guilty, not the host.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say the agent is adding to the host's words; that is why the host is guilty. But if you say the agent is going against his words, why is the host guilty? We learned: if an agent did his mission, the host is guilty; if he did not do his mission, the agent is guilty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the משנה proves the point. It shows that the host's guilt only makes sense if the שליח counts as 'adding' to the host's instruction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A known rule says that when a שליח carries out his mission, the sender is guilty of מעילה, and when he does not, the שליח alone is guilty. Since the host is guilty here, the שליח must have carried out the host's mission of one piece and simply added more. That is the 'מוסיף' view, so the לתך in our case should be sold.

keyTerms.meaning: Adding to his words: doing what he was told, plus extra
Going against his words: not doing the mission at all
But didn't we learn in a משנה: introduces a source that creates a difficulty
His mission, the job he was sent to do

phrases.english: It works well if you say
he is adding to his words
that is why the host is guilty of misusing הקדש.
But if you say
he is going against his words
why is the host guilty of misusing הקדש?
But didn't we learn:
An agent who carried out his mission
the host is guilty of misusing הקדש;
if he did not carry out his mission
the agent is guilty of misusing הקדש!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא מוֹסִיף עַל דְּבָרָיו הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the logic of the proof brought in Step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That a שליח who goes beyond his instructions is מוסיף על דבריו.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The host's guilt in the case from Step 9, combined with the rule that a sender is guilty only when his שליח carried out the mission.

steps.title: Rejection: the agent clearly separated the host's piece from his own
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the משנה may be a case where the שליח told the guests, 'Take one with the host's consent and one with mine,' and they took three.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Where the agent told them, 'Take one with the host's consent, and one with my consent,' and they took three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It says the משנה may describe a special case, so it does not settle our question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the שליח openly said that one piece is from the host, then he clearly did the host's mission for that piece, and the host is guilty for it either way. So the משנה tells us nothing about a regular case where the שליח just gave more without separating. The question from Step 8 is still unanswered, and Step 12 tries a different proof.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? Used to narrow a source to a special case
With my consent, on my own say-so
Three (Aramaic)

phrases.english: What case are we dealing with here?
Where he (the agent) said to them:
"Take one with the consent of the host,
and one with my consent,"
and they took three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Steps 9–10 by limiting the משנה to a special case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only this proof; it does not decide the question in the other direction.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed a regular case. The משנה can be read as a case where the שליח openly gave one piece in the host's name, so the host is guilty even if a שליח who adds is normally מעביר על דבריו.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה about the host and guests does not prove anything, because it may be a case where the שליח clearly gave one piece in the host's name.

steps.title: A new attempted proof: the widow who sold too much
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries a new proof from our משנה: if a widow's כתובה was a מנה and she sold property worth a מנה and a דינר for a מנה, her sale is void.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If her כתובה was one מנה, and she sold property worth a מנה and a דינר for a מנה, her sale is void.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a second attempt to answer the question, this time from our own משנה. Here it only quotes the case; the reasoning comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The widow was allowed to sell only a מנה's worth to collect her כתובה, but she sold a field worth a little more. That is like a שליח who sold more than he was told. The משנה says the whole sale is void, and the גמרא is about to use that for our question.

keyTerms.meaning: Her כתובה, the amount a wife collects when the marriage ends
A מנה, a sum of one hundred דינרים
A דינר, one coin
Her sale is void, not valid at all

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If her כתובה was one מנה,
phrases.notes: This is our own משנה, about a widow who sells her late husband's property to collect her כתובה.

phrases.english: and she sold property worth a מנה and a דינר for a מנה
her sale is void.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, starts a new attempt to settle the question from Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: The question from Step 8: whether a שליח who sells more than he was told is מוסיף or מעביר על דבריו.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה: a widow who sold property worth a מנה and a דינר for her מנה כתובה, where the sale is void.

steps.title: Reading the widow's case as a fair sale of too much land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the משנה as a widow who sold land worth a מנה and a דינר for its full price, a מנה and a דינר. Even though she offers to return the extra דינר to the heirs in land, the משנה rules that her whole sale is void.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't the case that she sold land worth a מנה and a דינר for a מנה and a דינר? And 'for a מנה' means 'to collect her own מנה.' And what does 'even' mean? Even if she says, 'I will give the דינר back to the heirs as a דינר's worth of land,' the משנה still teaches that her sale is void.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly how it is reading our משנה. Then it draws the proof: even with no loss to the heirs, the whole sale is cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The widow sells the heirs' land to collect her כתובה, so she is acting like a שליח. Here she sold more than she needed, a מנה and a דינר instead of just a מנה, and the price was fair. If she were only 'adding to' her mission, the sale should work at least for the מנה. Since the משנה says the whole sale is void, it seems that selling too much counts as 'going against' the mission.

keyTerms.meaning: What, is it not...? The גמרא's way of offering a reading it wants to prove
Her own מנה, the amount owed to her by her כתובה
The heirs of the husband, who own the property
Land, real estate
Her sale is void, cancelled completely

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'בְּמָנֶה' in the משנה sounds like the price of the sale. In this reading it is not the price. It means she sold in order to collect her מנה, and the real price was a מנה and a דינר.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this reading holds, it would settle the question from Step 8: a שליח who sells more than he was told goes against the sender, and nothing is sold.

phrases.english: What, is it not that she sold
property worth a מנה and a dinar for a מנה and a dinar,
and what does 'for a מנה' mean?
Her own מנה.
And what does 'even' mean?
Even if she says,
'I will return the dinar to the heirs
as a dinar's worth of land,'
phrases.notes: She would give them back land worth a דינר, so the heirs end up losing nothing at all.

phrases.english: and it teaches: her sale is void.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו דְּזַבֵּין שָׁוֶה מָנֶה וְדִינָר בְּמָנֶה וְדִינָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in Step 12 by explaining how the משנה must be read so that it answers the question of Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That a שליח who sells more than he was told 'goes against his words,' so the whole sale fails.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה: a widow whose כתובה was a מנה sold property worth a מנה and a דינר, and her sale is void even if she offers to return the dinar.

steps.title: The case is where she sold too cheaply
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן rejects the proof. The משנה is talking about a widow who sold land worth a מנה and a דינר for only a מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב נתן said: No, the case is where she lowered the price.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן pushes back on the proof. He reads the משנה differently, as a case where the widow undercharged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his reading, 'בְּמָנֶה' really is the price: land worth a מנה and a דינר was sold for just a מנה. The sale fails because of that bad deal, which hurts the heirs. So the משנה tells us nothing about a שליח who sold too much at a fair price, and this proof does not settle the question from Step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: Where she made it cheap, meaning she sold below the true value
No. Here it opens a rejection of the proposed reading

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the widow fails. Her sale may be void only because she undercharged, not because she sold more than she was sent to sell.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן:
phrases.english: רב הונא son of רב נתן said:
No, it is where she lowered the price.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן: לָא, בִּדְאוֹזֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading of the משנה offered in Step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only this proof from the משנה. It does not decide the question from Step 8 either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the sale was at a fair price. The משנה can be read as a sale below value, which fails for its own reason.
